tests.title: core.Tool exposes OutputSchema field while core.ToolWire excludes it
given: a tool definition with Name, Description, InputSchema, and OutputSchema
tests.when: t.Wire() is invoked to produce a core.ToolWire projection
then: t.OutputSchema is accessible as *schema.Schema
the resulting ToolWire has Name, Description, InputSchema, and ConstrainedSampling matching t
ToolWire has no OutputSchema field
tests.pseudocode: s := schema.Object(schema.Prop("key", schema.String())); t := core.Tool{Name: "test", OutputSchema: s}; w := t.Wire(); assert t.OutputSchema == s; assert reflect.TypeOf(w).FieldByName("OutputSchema").Index == nil

tests.title: Tools with nil OutputSchema can be registered and executed normally
given: an Agent or tool registry and a tool created with OutputSchema left nil
tests.when: the tool is registered and executed with valid arguments
then: registration succeeds without error
tool execution returns a valid ToolResult with OK true
tests.pseudocode: t := core.Tool{Name: "echo", Execute: func(ctx context.Context, in json.RawMessage) core.ToolResult { return core.OKResult(map[string]any{"ok": true}) }}; assert t.OutputSchema == nil; res := t.Execute(ctx, nil); assert res.OK == true

tests.title: Provider wire requests remain byte-identical regardless of OutputSchema presence
given: the canonical request fixture and wire golden tests
tests.when: for any tool set with arbitrary combinations of nil or populated OutputSchema declarations
then: serialized request bodies across Anthropic, Google, Ollama, OpenAI, and OpenAI Responses wire formats match golden request fixtures byte-for-byte
tests.pseudocode: for req in genRequestsWithArbitraryOutputSchemas(): for provider in [anthropic, google, ollama, openai, openairesponses]: body := provider.Marshal(req.Tools); golden := loadGolden(provider); assert bytes.Equal(body, golden)

tests.title: MCP pool adaptor maps valid MCP tool outputSchema to core.Tool.OutputSchema
given: an MCP server tool definition with a valid JSON schema outputSchema
tests.when: the pool adapts the MCP tool into a core.Tool
then: core.Tool.OutputSchema is non-nil
core.Tool.OutputSchema reflects the properties and types defined by the server outputSchema
tests.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "calc", OutputSchema: map[string]any{"type": "object", "properties": map[string]any{"value": map[string]any{"type": "number"}}, "required": []any{"value"}}}; adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__calc"); assert adapted.OutputSchema != nil; assert adapted.OutputSchema.Type == schema.TypeObject

tests.title: Malformed MCP tool outputSchema is dropped with a SeverityError diagnostic without failing connection
given: an MCP server tool definition with an invalid or unparseable outputSchema
tests.when: the pool adapts the MCP tool into a core.Tool
then: adapted tool has OutputSchema == nil
pool diagnostics slice contains a SeverityError diagnostic naming the server and tool
connection remains open and tool is successfully adapted
tests.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "broken", OutputSchema: "not a valid schema object"}; adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__broken"); assert adapted.OutputSchema == nil; diags := pool.Diagnostics(); assert len(diags) > 0; assert diags[0].Severity == diag.SeverityError; assert strings.Contains(diags[0].Message, "broken")

tests.title: MCP tool definition with omitted outputSchema sets OutputSchema to nil with no diagnostics
given: an MCP server tool definition without an outputSchema field
tests.when: the pool adapts the MCP tool into a core.Tool
then: adapted tool has OutputSchema == nil
no diagnostics are appended to the pool diagnostics
tests.pseudocode: toolDef := &mcp.Tool{Name: "simple", OutputSchema: nil}; initialDiags := len(pool.Diagnostics()); adapted := pool.adapt(conn, toolDef, "srv__simple"); assert adapted.OutputSchema == nil; assert len(pool.Diagnostics()) == initialDiags

tests.title: MCP tool execution with object StructuredContent passes map directly to ToolResult.Data
given: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with StructuredContent as map[string]any
tests.when: the adapted tool's Execute function is called
then: ToolResult.Data equals the StructuredContent map directly without nesting under 'structured'
tests.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{StructuredContent: map[string]any{"temperature": 72.5, "units": "F"}}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert reflect.DeepEqual(res.Data, map[string]any{"temperature": 72.5, "units": "F"})

tests.title: MCP tool execution with non-object StructuredContent wraps value in map under key value
given: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with primitive StructuredContent (e.g. integer, string, or array)
tests.when: the adapted tool's Execute function is called
then: ToolResult.Data is map[string]any{"value": StructuredContent}
tests.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{StructuredContent: 42}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert reflect.DeepEqual(res.Data, map[string]any{"value": 42})

tests.title: MCP tool execution without StructuredContent returns fallback map with text and content
given: an adapted MCP tool whose invocation returns CallToolResult with nil StructuredContent and text content
tests.when: the adapted tool's Execute function is called
then: ToolResult.Data contains key 'text' with joined text and key 'content' with raw content slice
tests.pseudocode: mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{Content: []mcp.Content{&mcp.TextContent{Text: "hello world"}}, StructuredContent: nil}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert res.Data["text"] == "hello world"; assert res.Data["content"] != nil

tests.title: MCP tool execution concatenates all text content blocks into ToolResult.Text
given: an adapted MCP tool
tests.when: for any MCP tool execution returning arbitrary content blocks
then: ToolResult.Text equals the concatenated text from all text content blocks
tests.pseudocode: for blocks in genContentBlocks(): mockConn.callResult = &mcp.CallToolResult{Content: blocks}; res := adapted.Execute(ctx, rawJSON); assert res.Text == joinTextBlocks(blocks)

tests.title: read_file declares OutputSchema as OneOf text and image read schemas
given: the built-in read_file tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is a schema.OneOf schema with two branch schemas
first branch is an object with required properties 'content' (string) and 'encoding' (string)
second branch is an object with required properties 'note' (string), 'mime_type' (string), 'width' (integer), and 'height' (integer)
tests.pseudocode: t := tools.ReadFileTool(ws); s := t.OutputSchema; assert s != nil; assert len(s.OneOf) == 2; textBranch := s.OneOf[0]; assert textBranch.Properties["content"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert textBranch.Properties["encoding"].Type == schema.TypeString; imgBranch := s.OneOf[1]; assert imgBranch.Properties["mime_type"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert imgBranch.Properties["width"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: write_file and edit_file declare their respective OutputSchema
given: the built-in write_file and edit_file tools
tests.when: their OutputSchema definitions are inspected
then: write_file OutputSchema is an object schema with 'written' (boolean) and 'bytes' (integer)
edit_file OutputSchema is an object schema with 'edits_applied' (integer)
tests.pseudocode: w := tools.WriteFileTool(ws); assert w.OutputSchema.Properties["written"].Type == schema.TypeBoolean; assert w.OutputSchema.Properties["bytes"].Type == schema.TypeInteger; e := tools.EditFileTool(ws); assert e.OutputSchema.Properties["edits_applied"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: list_files and find_files declare their respective OutputSchema
given: the built-in list_files and find_files tools
tests.when: their OutputSchema definitions are inspected
then: list_files OutputSchema is an object with required 'entries' (array of strings), required 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'note' (string)
find_files OutputSchema is an object with required 'files' (array of strings), required 'truncated' (boolean), and optional 'marker' (string)
tests.pseudocode: l := tools.ListFilesTool(ws); assert l.OutputSchema.Properties["entries"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert l.OutputSchema.Properties["truncated"].Type == schema.TypeBoolean; f := tools.FindFilesTool(ws); assert f.OutputSchema.Properties["files"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert f.OutputSchema.Properties["marker"].Type == schema.TypeString

tests.title: search_files declares OutputSchema matching search result shape
given: the built-in search_files tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'matches', 'truncated', 'files_searched', and optional 'note'
'matches' is an array of objects having 'file' (string), 'line' (integer), 'text' (string), and optional 'context_before' and 'context_after' string arrays
tests.pseudocode: s := tools.SearchFilesTool(ws); assert s.OutputSchema != nil; assert s.OutputSchema.Properties["matches"].Type == schema.TypeArray; item := s.OutputSchema.Properties["matches"].Items; assert item.Properties["file"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert item.Properties["line"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: file_outline declares OutputSchema matching outline result shape
given: the built-in file_outline tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'file', 'backend', 'declarations', and 'listed'
'file' is an object containing 'path', 'lang', 'backend', and 'decls' array of declaration objects
tests.pseudocode: o := tools.FileOutlineTool(ws); assert o.OutputSchema != nil; assert o.OutputSchema.Properties["backend"].Type == schema.TypeString; fileProp := o.OutputSchema.Properties["file"]; assert fileProp.Properties["decls"].Type == schema.TypeArray; declItem := fileProp.Properties["decls"].Items; assert declItem.Properties["name"].Type == schema.TypeString

tests.title: find_symbol declares OutputSchema matching symbol answer shape
given: the built-in find_symbol tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'symbols', 'truncated', 'backends', 'files_indexed', and optional 'note', 'partial', and 'partial_reason'
'symbols' is an array of symbol objects having 'name', 'kind', 'path', 'start_line', 'end_line', and optional 'signature', 'container', 'exported', 'score'
tests.pseudocode: fs := tools.FindSymbolTool(ws, index); assert fs.OutputSchema != nil; assert fs.OutputSchema.Properties["symbols"].Type == schema.TypeArray; symItem := fs.OutputSchema.Properties["symbols"].Items; assert symItem.Properties["name"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert symItem.Properties["kind"].Type == schema.TypeString

tests.title: find_references declares OutputSchema matching reference result shape
given: the built-in find_references tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema with 'target', 'sites', 'backend', 'partial', 'truncated', 'packages_checked', 'errors', and 'result'
'sites' is an array of objects having 'path', 'line', 'text', and optional 'container', 'kind'
tests.pseudocode: fr := tools.FindReferencesTool(ws); assert fr.OutputSchema != nil; assert fr.OutputSchema.Properties["sites"].Type == schema.TypeArray; siteItem := fr.OutputSchema.Properties["sites"].Items; assert siteItem.Properties["path"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert siteItem.Properties["line"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: Subprocess tools share OutputSchema and populate matching Data on failure outcomes
given: the built-in subprocess tools execute, run_command, and powershell
tests.when: their OutputSchema definitions are checked, and a command exits non-zero
then: all three tools share the same OutputSchema containing 'output' (string), 'exit_code' (integer), and 'outcome' (enum: ok, exit, signal, timeout, abort)
ToolResult.Data contains 'output', 'exit_code', and 'outcome' on non-zero exit and validates against OutputSchema
tests.pseudocode: ex := tools.ExecuteTool(); rc := tools.RunCommandTool(); ps := tools.PowerShellTool(); assert ex.OutputSchema == rc.OutputSchema && rc.OutputSchema == ps.OutputSchema; res := rc.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"exit 3"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Data["exit_code"] == 3; assert res.Data["outcome"] == "exit"; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(rc.OutputSchema, ord) == nil

tests.title: fetch_url declares OutputSchema matching fetch result metadata
given: the built-in fetch_url tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema with required 'status', 'url', 'content_type', 'headers', 'truncated', and optional 'binary', 'bytes'
tests.pseudocode: fu := tools.FetchURLTool(); assert fu.OutputSchema != nil; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["status"].Type == schema.TypeInteger; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["url"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert fu.OutputSchema.Properties["headers"].Type == schema.TypeObject

tests.title: code_search declares OutputSchema matching indexed search results
given: the built-in code_search tool
tests.when: its OutputSchema is inspected
then: OutputSchema is an object schema containing 'files', 'truncated', 'note', 'partial', 'partial_reason', 'symbol_sources', 'files_indexed', 'dirty_files', and 'skipped'
'files' is an array of file match objects, and 'skipped' is an object with binary, oversized, too_many_trigrams, and too_small integer properties
tests.pseudocode: cs := codesearch.Tool(idx); assert cs.OutputSchema != nil; assert cs.OutputSchema.Properties["files"].Type == schema.TypeArray; assert cs.OutputSchema.Properties["skipped"].Type == schema.TypeObject; skipProps := cs.OutputSchema.Properties["skipped"].Properties; assert skipProps["binary"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

then: OutputSchema is an object schema with properties 'result' (string) and 'turns' (integer)
tests.pseudocode: sa := subagent.Tool(factory, opts); assert sa.OutputSchema != nil; assert sa.OutputSchema.Properties["result"].Type == schema.TypeString; assert sa.OutputSchema.Properties["turns"].Type == schema.TypeInteger

tests.title: Conformance suite validates ToolResult.Data against OutputSchema for all built-in tools on success
given: an initialized workspace with sample files and every built-in tool registered
tests.when: each built-in tool is executed with valid arguments producing OK == true
then: each tool returns res.OK == true
each tool produces res.Data != nil
schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data)) returns nil with no validation issues
tests.pseudocode: for tool in allBuiltinTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, validArgs[tool.Name]); assert res.OK == true; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ord) == nil

tests.title: Built-in tools return invalid_arguments error on malformed JSON or invalid parameter values
given: each built-in tool
tests.when: the tool is executed with malformed JSON input or values violating argument schema
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is equal to 'invalid_arguments'
tests.pseudocode: for tool in allBuiltinTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{malformed`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "invalid_arguments"

tests.title: File and outline tools return path_not_allowed when target path exceeds workspace boundary
given: built-in tools operating on filesystem paths (read_file, write_file, edit_file, list_files, find_files, file_outline, find_symbol)
tests.when: invoked with path '../outside/secret.txt' or absolute path outside workspace
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is equal to 'path_not_allowed'
tests.pseudocode: for tool in fileTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"../../secret"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "path_not_allowed"

tests.title: read_file, edit_file, and file_outline return not_a_file when targeting directories or non-regular files
given: a directory existing in the workspace
tests.when: read_file, edit_file, or file_outline is called with the directory path
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is equal to 'not_a_file'
tests.pseudocode: for tool in [read_file, edit_file, file_outline]: res := tool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"existing_dir"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "not_a_file"

tests.title: Built-in tools return aborted when executed with an already cancelled context
given: each cancellable built-in tool and a cancelled context.Context
tests.when: the tool is executed with the cancelled context
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is equal to 'aborted'
tests.pseudocode: ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); cancel(); for tool in cancellableTools: res := tool.Execute(ctx, validArgs[tool.Name]); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "aborted"

tests.title: Subprocess shell tools on failure return command_exit or exec_failed and validate Data against OutputSchema
given: the execute and run_command tools
tests.when: invoked with a command that exits with non-zero status or an unexecutable binary
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is 'command_exit' or 'exec_failed'
schema.Validate(tool.OutputSchema, ordered) returns nil for res.Data
tests.pseudocode: res := runCmd.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"sh -c 'exit 1'"}`)); assert res.OK == false; assert res.Error == "command_exit"; ord := jsonx.ToOrdered(res.Data); assert schema.Validate(runCmd.OutputSchema, ord) == nil; res2 := runCmd.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"command":"/nonexistent_bin_xyz"}`)); assert res2.OK == false; assert res2.Error == "exec_failed"

tests.title: read_file and fetch_url return offset_past_end, scheme_not_allowed, or address_not_allowed on out-of-range or forbidden requests
given: workspace with a 10-byte file and SSRF guard
tests.when: read_file is called with offset 999, fetch_url is called with scheme 'ftp://', or fetch_url targets private IP 127.0.0.1
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is one of 'offset_past_end', 'scheme_not_allowed', or 'address_not_allowed' matching the induced condition
tests.pseudocode: res1 := readFile.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"f.txt","offset":999}`)); assert res1.OK == false && res1.Error == "offset_past_end"; res2 := fetchUrl.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"url":"ftp://example.com"}`)); assert res2.OK == false && res2.Error == "scheme_not_allowed"; res3 := fetchUrl.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"url":"http://127.0.0.1"}`)); assert res3.OK == false && res3.Error == "address_not_allowed"

tests.title: File operation tools and subagent return documented error codes on respective failures
given: error-inducing conditions: read-only file for write, mismatched old_str for edit, unlistable directory, failing subagent runner
tests.when: the respective tools are executed
then: res.OK is false
res.Error is one of 'read_failed', 'write_failed', 'edit_precondition', 'edit_failed', 'list_failed', 'outline_failed', or 'subagent_failed' matching the induced failure
tests.pseudocode: resEdit := editTool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"path":"f.txt","edits":[{"old_str":"not_there","new_str":"x"}]}`)); assert resEdit.OK == false && resEdit.Error == "edit_precondition"; resSub := subagentTool.Execute(ctx, json.RawMessage(`{"task":"fail"}`)); assert resSub.OK == false && resSub.Error == "subagent_failed"
